original_question: Fix integers N ≥ 1, d ≥ 2, and D ≥ 1. There is a constant C(N, d, D) such that for all degree d morphisms f : PN → PN defined over a number field K of degree [K : Q] = D, the number of K-rational preperiodic points is uniformly bounded,  # PrePer f, PN (K) ≤ C(N, d, D).
target_in_paper: Section 4, Conjecture 4.2, the "Dynamical Uniform Boundedness Conjecture" of Morton-Silverman. Your draft is essentially this conjecture itself, rather than the broader family version in Section 4.1. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
correct_elements: The draft already matches the paper's main statement in Section 4 almost verbatim: it fixes integers N >= 1, d >= 2, and D >= 1; quantifies over degree-d morphisms f : P^N -> P^N defined over number fields K with [K:Q] = D; and asks for a uniform bound on the number of K-rational preperiodic points. That is exactly Conjecture 4.2. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
missing_details: The notation PrePer(f, P^N(K)) should be defined explicitly: PrePer(f,S) = {alpha in S : f^n(alpha) = f^m(alpha) for some integers n > m >= 0}. This is given in Definition 2.1. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

The ambient space P^N(K) should be identified as the set of K-rational points of projective N-space P^N. Section 3 defines both P^N and P^N(K). ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, one should say what a degree-d morphism of P^N means in the paper's setup: a self-map given by N+1 homogeneous polynomials of the same degree d with coefficients in K, with no common factor, and with empty indeterminacy locus (equivalently, an element of End_d^N(K)). ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

It helps to state explicitly that the bound is uniform in both K and f once N, d, and D are fixed; i.e. C(N,d,D) depends only on those three integers. This is the point of Conjecture 4.2. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

If the question is meant to stand alone, it should say that the count is over K-rational preperiodic points P in P^N(K), not over all geometric preperiodic points in P^N(Kbar). ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

For motivation/context, the conjecture is posed only after Northcott's theorem, which says that for each fixed f over a number field K, the set PrePer(f, P^N(K)) is finite. The conjecture asks whether this finiteness can be made uniform in families with fixed N, d, and D. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

No nilpotency hypothesis, asymptotic clause such as 'for all sufficiently large m,' or extra homogeneity condition beyond the homogeneous coordinate description of a morphism appears in the target statement; adding such conditions would drift away from the paper's formulation. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
refined_question:
Does the Dynamical Uniform Boundedness Conjecture hold? Namely: for fixed integers N >= 1, d >= 2, and D >= 1, does there exist a constant C(N,d,D) such that for every number field K with [K:Q] = D and every degree-d morphism f : P^N -> P^N defined over K, one has
#PrePer(f, P^N(K)) <= C(N,d,D),
where P^N(K) is the set of K-rational points of projective N-space and
PrePer(f, P^N(K)) := {P in P^N(K) : f^n(P) = f^m(P) for some integers n > m >= 0}? ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
justification: The nearest official target is Conjecture 4.2 in Section 4, not a neighboring problem. The draft already reproduces its mathematical content almost exactly. The only real gaps are stand-alone notation and setup: Definition 2.1 supplies the meaning of preperiodic and the notation PrePer(f,S), while Section 3 supplies the meanings of P^N(K), degree, homogeneous coordinates, morphism, and End_d^N(K). The surrounding context in Theorem 4.1 shows why the conjecture is asked: Northcott gives finiteness for each individual map, and Conjecture 4.2 asks for a bound uniform in all maps over degree-D number fields. The broader Conjecture 4.9 in Section 4.1 only implies Conjecture 4.2, so it should not replace it here. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
